evidence_layer: synthetic memory oracle: the original ARM bytes at 0x1f3ce0 executed over staged .bss cells, hash tables, CObjectGM chains, scan lists and the room instance chain; its tail jump lands in the ORIGINAL Variable_GetValue_Direct @0x1f3b8c, with identical GET_RValue / InternalGetYYVar / builtin-getter stubs on both arms; NOT device execution

linked_callee.arm: real link on the claim arm; original bytes on the judge arm (not a stub)

got_rewritten.0x3edc40: builtin-variable table base -> the oracle heap table (10000 entries do not fit the image .bss)

covered: dispatch: sel == -3 / sel < 0 / sel > 99999 / 0..99999, decided by the original's own three compares
room path: *(*(0x54298c))+0x80 head, next at +0x178 loaded before the gates, both liveness bytes
id path: ms_ID2InstanceE bucket = id & table mask, 8 B buckets, node {+4 next, +8 id, +0xc inst}, full 32-bit key, only +0x68 gated (+0x69 deliberately not read)
object path: g_ObjectHash is a POINTER VARIABLE (the extra deref at 0x1f3e84), CObjectGM +0xd0 chain {+0 next, +8 inst}, both liveness bytes
both fallback lists (0x542a64 / 0x542a4c): 12 B {items, pad, count}, count <= 0 skipped, 4 B elements, ancestor walk via +0x48 comparing +0x18, both liveness bytes, scan order
return contract: Direct's return passed through (tail jump), 0 on every failure exit
failure semantics: return 0 + flag 0x75505c = 1 + out byte-identical to the caller's preset (0x00FFFFFF tag kept)
varid / arrindex passthrough: slot deltas, builtin dispatch, the [10000,99999] gap, negative varid, INT_MIN/INT_MAX arrindex
Variable_GetValue_Direct runs for real on both arms
not_covered: GET_RValue@0xd13bc semantics - stubbed identically on both arms, NOT recovered; a green run does not prove it
YYObjectBase::InternalGetYYVar@0x196a70 - stubbed; every staged instance has a non-NULL variable table so the lazy path is never entered
builtin-variable getter semantics - stubbed identical page
the class identity of the two fallback lists and their +4 field (never read by this body) - cards/Variable_GetValue.c open 1
varid in [10000,99999] reaching Direct with a negative slot index: the arithmetic is pinned, whether the name table can emit such an id is not (card open 2)
device behaviour: this is a synthetic-memory oracle over the original bytes, not execution on a phone
observability: every staged instance has +0x24 = 1 (a non-empty variable table), so a successful resolve always reaches GET_RValue or the builtin getter - that is what makes the resolved instance observable on BOTH arms without reading a register the translation could fake
every instance has its own 16 B-slot window of region S, so a G line slot delta encodes (instance, slot) even when the slot index is negative
a failure case cannot say WHICH instance the original had picked before it gave up - there is nothing to observe

staging_geometry.shared: the write program is one description interpreted by both arms; only the region bases differ (the judge arm uses the image's own .bss cells for the six globals, the claim arm its own symbols)

findings: the body has TWO indirection levels on the object hash and on the room, not three: 0x1f3e84 / 0x1f3f14 are the single extra load that turns the pointer variable into the structure.  The first translation added a third level on the room path (a "holder" whose word 0 is the CRoom*) and the differential caught it as five room cases where the original returned 0/flag 1 while the claim arm resolved an instance - the staging was symmetric, the C body was not.
the two fallback lists are gated by a SIGNED count compare (ble on +8), so a negative count skips the list exactly like a zero one (case E14).

the id path really reads only +0x68: case C5 resolves a deactivated instance by id, while C4 fails on a destroyed one; the mutant that adds the +0x69 test to the id path is caught by exactly that pair.
the arithmetical "equal" bit of scan list 2 (subs/rsbs/adcs) collapses to (sel == index) - the translation keeps the flag chain and the collapse is stated at the adcs line.
